style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a small mechanical assembly on a weathered concrete garage floor. A wall-mounted advanced utility meter housing with a round glass dome and a blank unmarked face, below it a detached current-transformer clamp with open jaws and a short coiled wire. The meter body has a row of tiny raised dots around its rim representing hourly intervals. One directional key light from the left rakes across the matte surfaces, throwing long contact shadows. Palette: bone white, graphite, deep pine green. Asymmetrical composition with the meter off-centre left and the clamp lower right, generous negative space. No text, no numerals, no display, no labels, no markings.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI elements, numerals
rationale: A clay render builds the two competing instruments as a small physical assembly, making the hourly-row meter and circuit-level clamp legible without any screen text that could turn to rubble. It avoids the rejected photorealism and lettering problem by using matte, unmarked surfaces. The treatment also allows a split arrangement that states the dual nature of the two tools without needing labels.
cue: Your meter bills from hourly rows
subject: An unmarked wall-mounted advanced utility meter with a sealed round glass dome and a detached current-transformer clamp on the garage floor beneath it.
core_thesis: The advanced meter on the wall already logs the house hour by hour and hands that record back at least once a day, so the free file settles seasonal cost while the only things a panel clamp adds are a finer sample rate and the name of the circuit.
core_conflict: The free utility meter file answers cost and trend questions at hourly resolution but cannot identify which circuit drew power; a panel clamp provides that circuit-level granularity, forcing owners to choose between free coarse data and purchased fine-grained monitoring.
composition: extreme asymmetry with meter upper-left and clamp lower-right, raking light diagonal

review.depicts: A small glass-domed device mounted on a white bracket attached to a concrete wall at upper left, with a coiled cable below it and a green plastic block with prongs lying on the cracked concrete floor at lower right.
review.reason: The frame shows a wall-mounted metering device with a sealed round dome and a separate clamp-like sensor on the floor, which is the article's own object pair (advanced meter vs. add-on clamp), though the clamp reads as an ambiguous green block and the meter looks more vintage than advanced.
